project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 275 (System rejects a dreaming run when the pool holds fewer than 20 worlds, which returns a pool_too_thin error message)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 275 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): a *ladder-floor* precondition, `rejects_thin_pool(world_count, gate=20)` (and a `PoolTooThinError`), that refuses to start a dreaming run when the pool holds fewer than 20 worlds. This is the precondition that feature 270 (the pool held fixed for the cycle, already implemented) deliberately does NOT carry: feature 270's subject is a cycle that is *running* and must not have its pool moved underneath it (it carries `pool_frozen`), while feature 275 is a precondition on a run that has *not started* — docs/alpha-engine- prd.md §12.1's ladder floor ("below 20 worlds: do not run dreaming; fixed exploration; accumulate history"). The two sentences have different repairs and different greppable codes, and the workspace's error-vocabulary discipline (no member imports another; a shared helper that raises another feature's error type defeats the caller's `except`) forbids feature 275 from borrowing feature 270's `pool_frozen`. So feature 275 adds its own code, `pool_too_thin`, and its own error class, in the same member, as a sibling of feature 270's classes under the same `DreamingError` base — not a new member, not a new component, not a new table. The refusal is a *judgment over a count the caller already has*, not a count the feature performs: the dreaming member already reads the pool's size (feature 270's hold records `world_count`, and `pool_commitment` returns it), so feature 275 takes the figure as an argument — the same verdict-gate shape feature 187's headline refusal and feature 230's admission gate take — and refuses when the figure is below the gate. The gate is a parameter, defaulting to 20 (the §12.1 floor), validated to be a non-negative whole number so a gate that is not a world count cannot silently admit or block a run. The refusal message opens with the code `pool_too_thin`, states the figure and the gate, states the repair (do not run dreaming; accumulate history / grow the pool), and names the governing document (§12.1). No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; no new `@register` component is added (feature 270's single `"dreaming"` component is untouched); the member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/<member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.bootstrap, app.modules.artifacts, app.modules.dreaming). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/dreaming/tests/`). Stdlib-only computation is the norm for a member that fronts already-computed values, so feature 275's floor adds no third-party dependency: it is a comparison over an integer. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md / docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition (a builder that raises would take composition down for every unrelated feature, so a builder returns `None` for a deployment that names no store), member-owned tables created lazily beside the only module that writes them (never in the shared migration chain, which is order-sensitive and excluded from this feature's file claim), and the error-vocabulary discipline that no member imports another and a shared helper that raises another feature's error type defeats the caller's `except` (translate at the seam). Feature 270 already lives in this member (packages/dreaming: layout.py restates the pool spelling, cycle.py is the CycleFreeze store, errors.py holds DreamingError / FreezeRequestError / PoolFrozenError, __init__.py re-exports and fires `@register("dreaming")`, seat src/app/modules/dreaming). Feature 275 is a sibling within that member, not a new member.

category.name: Dreaming Loop & Meta-Selection
category.feature: System rejects a dreaming run when the pool holds fewer than 20 worlds, which returns a pool_too_thin error message.

project_specification.integration_points: The refusal is a pure judgment over a world count the caller already has, added to the dreaming member (packages/dreaming) as a sibling of feature 270. It is reached directly from the member (`from dreaming import reject_thin_pool, PoolTooThinError, POOL_TOO_THIN_CODE`), the way feature 270's `open_cycle_freeze` and its errors are, and — for a composed application — through the existing seat (`app.modules.dreaming`), which already hands back feature 270's single CycleFreeze component; feature 275 adds no second component and edits no seat. The count the judgment reads is the pool's size, which the member already computes (feature 270's `pool_commitment` returns `(digest, world_count)` and the hold records `world_count`), so the caller obtains the figure from the same member it asks to judge, and the judgment never counts the pool itself. The gate (default 20) is a keyword of the refusal so a deployment may set the floor differently; it is validated to be a non-negative whole number.
project_specification.constraints: - Feature 275 is a precondition on a run that has NOT started, and is deliberately NOT feature 270's `pool_frozen`: it must use its own code, `pool_too_thin`, and its own error class, `PoolTooThinError`, a sibling of feature 270's classes under the shared `DreamingError` base. It must NOT reuse `pool_frozen`, `PoolFrozenError`, or `FreezeRequestError` for the thin-pool refusal, and feature 270's existing behaviour, messages, codes and tests must be untouched. - No member imports another. The count the judgment reads is obtained from the dreaming member's own existing surface (the pool size the member already computes), never from a sibling member's import. - No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited. No new `@register` component is added — feature 270's single `"dreaming"` component is untouched, and feature 275 adds no component, no table, and no seat export. - The refusal is a judgment over a count, not a count the feature performs: `reject_thin_pool(world_count, *, gate=20)` takes the figure as an argument and does not open a database or read the pool itself. - The gate defaults to 20 (docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §12.1's ladder floor) and is validated to be a non-negative whole number. - The refusal message opens with the code `pool_too_thin`, states the figure and the gate, states the repair (do not run dreaming; fixed exploration; accumulate history / grow the pool), and names the governing document (§12.1). - All existing tests in the dreaming member (packages/dreaming/tests) and in tests/ must stay green. The member's own suite must be run explicitly (it is not graded by the bare `uv run pytest` gate). - Do not edit the order-sensitive shared files: src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/versions/**, alembic/versions/**.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the code and the class. Add `POOL_TOO_THIN_CODE = "pool_too_thin"` and a `PoolTooThinError(DreamingError)` to the dreaming member's error vocabulary as a sibling of feature 270's two classes, following the same repair-split discipline (the repair for a thin pool is not to re-send a corrected ask but to grow the pool / not run dreaming). Add `reject_thin_pool(world_count, *, gate=20)` — a pure function that validates `world_count` is a non-negative whole number and `gate` is a non-negative whole number, and raises `PoolTooThinError` (message opening with `pool_too_thin`, stating the figure, the gate, the repair, and §12.1) when `world_count < gate`. Re-export both from the member `__init__.py` alongside feature 270's existing names. No new component, table, or seat export.

Phase 2 — the tests. Add a suite in packages/dreaming/tests asserting: the floor refuses below 20 (e.g. 0, 5, 19) with `pool_too_thin` and admits at and above the gate (20, 45); the gate is a parameter (a custom gate changes the verdict) and is validated (a negative or non-integer gate, and a negative or non-integer count, are refused in the ask's own vocabulary); `PoolTooThinError` is a `DreamingError` and a sibling of feature 270's classes (not a subclass of `PoolFrozenError` or `FreezeRequestError`); the message opens with `pool_too_thin`, names the figure and gate, states the repair, and cites §12.1; and feature 270's vocabulary is unchanged (the existing `test_the_member_does_not_carry_the_ladder_floor` assertion in test_errors.py is updated to reflect that `pool_too_thin` now exists as the code constant, while `PoolTooThinError` remains a feature-275 sibling — or, if that test's intent was to pin the *absence* of the floor in feature 270's own path, it is preserved and a separate feature-275 test pins the presence).

Phase 3 — verify. Run the dreaming member's own suite (`uv run pytest packages/dreaming/tests`) and the repository-level suite (`uv run pytest tests/`) — both, since the member suite is not graded by the bare gate — and confirm all pass. Lint only the changed files against a sibling (the repo lint is red on main). Confirm feature 270's behaviour and tests are untouched.
